pageCache.pageTitle: Hampstead Norreys Primary School | Hampstead Norreys Primary  |  Berkshire, UK
pageCache.text:
We are a small, friendly village primary school, who believe in providing the best opportunities for our children of all ages and abilities. We strongly feel that we “achieve more together” and can really make a difference in our children’s lives by building a partnership with our families. Our children demonstrate outstanding behaviour and really are a joy to teach. Our staff are fully involved in the daily life of the school to ensure that our children get the most out of their learning, enjoy their school and make a positive contribution to our community. Please come and visit our school to find out more.
Hampstead Norreys Church of England Primary School and The Ilsleys Primary School are now federated. We had a successful collaboration for nearly four years and naturally progressed onto federation. The school shares a Headteacher, Miss K.House as well as having an established leadership team that work together for both schools. They meet fortnightly and plan and work on various aspects of school improvement. The links between the two schools are very strong as a result of this, staff training takes place every week where both schools come together. Both schools plan and organise ‘challenge’ days where the children from both schools go across to each others school for a different learning experience. There is a school minibus which helps with the transportation of the children. Both schools have a fun, family orientated feel to them where children love learning in an environment that is nurturing and caring. The staff are dedicated to ensuring all our children get the best education they can as well as feeling cared for and valued as people. We do an excellent job in preparing our children for the future which makes these two schools wonderful places to learn.
Contact the school office to arrange a visit on 01635 201371 and we will be delighted to see you.
Executive Headteacher

pageCache.text:
Our Federation’s Ethos and Approach – SEND
The Ilsleys and Hampstead Norreys Federation believe in everyone working together to ensure that our school is a happy and welcoming place where children and adults can develop into confident and successful learners who are ready to meet the challenges of the future. By consistently focusing on the quality of teaching and learning, all groups of children are given the opportunity to develop and meet their potential including those who have been identified as having additional needs.
The four broad ‘areas of need’ are Communication and Interaction, Cognition and Learning, Social, Emotional and Mental Health Difficulties, and Sensory and Physical Needs. At The Ilsleys and Hampstead Norreys Federation, we embrace the fact that every child is different, and, therefore, the educational needs of every child is different; this is certainly the case for children with Special Educational Needs.
The Definitions of SEN and Disability
To ensure best outcomes possible for the children, the planning, organisation and management of education for SEND pupils is delivered in accordance to The SEND Code of Practice for 0-25 Year Olds, where the definition of SEND is stated as follows:
‘A child or young person has SEN if they have a learning difficulty or disability which calls for special educational provision to be made for him or her.

pageCache.pageTitle: Anti-Bullying Ambassadors | Hampstead Norreys Primary School
pageCache.text:
Anti-Bullying Ambassadors
We are delighted to have received the Anti-Bullying Accreditation from West Berkshire Council. This means that we have demonstrated clear evidence to show how we promote positive friendships, use peer mentoring systems in school, raise the profile of bullying and consider links with our own local community. We understand that bullying can happen to any person at any time and all of our children, parents, staff and governors are committed to ensuring we maintain an anti-bullying culture in our fantastic school.
Currently, we are working with the anti-bullying ambassadors at our federated school, The Ilsleys, to create a programme of events and activities to help promote kindness, boost self-esteem, help raise awareness of bullying and offer support to others.
We have an anti-bullying day programmed in on the 17th May, as well as termly Worship sessions, led by our anti-bullying ambassadors.

Thom Thomasson – Foundation Govenor
“Our family have lived in Hampstead Norreys for 4 years. We have one son at the village school. I have been a Christian since I was a child in various churches and in 2002 I took a year off work to study theology in Oxford. As a Foundation Governor my role is to strengthen the ties between the school and the parish and ensure that the Christian vision and founding principles of the school are core to everything that takes place within it. As part of that role I meet with the Little Oaks Committee and get involved with all apsects of Religious Education, Worship and SIAMS inspections. SIAMS Stands for Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools. If you would like to know more on any aspect of my role please feel free to ask. I can be contacted via the school office.”

At Hampstead Norreys and The Ilsleys Federation, we believe that all pupils have the ability to love Maths. We work hard to develop a growth mindset in children and a ‘can do’ attitude to Mathematics. We believe that, through quality first teaching, regular practise, collaborative learning and immediate intervention that all children have the potential to ‘go deeper’ and broaden their understanding of mathematical concepts.
We understand the importance of Mathematics in the wider world and encourage pupils to be reflective about how key concepts can be used in real life. We encourage them to make connections in their learning between different concepts and believe that all pupils should have the opportunity to develop, fluency, reasoning and problem-solving skills. We believe that, after developing true fluency, children need the opportunity to show that they can apply their knowledge and then move on even further to prove they have mastered the concept through detailed explanations.
Pupils in our school are reflective learners. Meta-cognition, especially working systematically and showing good reasoning skills, are at the heart of our Maths learning. The pupils in KS2 are keen to record their learning and the strategies they have used in their learning diaries. These provide a good foundation for when key concepts are re-visited across the year.
In terms of assessment, we have developed our curriculum to allow teachers and learners to achieve a secure and deep understanding of each mathematical concept. Key objectives are re-visited each term and built on throughout the year. This is evidenced in our assessment rubric. It is designed to give us the opportunity to address key points individually, ensure that children have a secure and deep understanding of those points, before offering the opportunity to ‘go deeper’ within them. Our aim is for all pupils to master the full Mathematics curriculum for their age range.
